minutes.headline: Assessors re-elected their chair after a resident urged new leadership over the abatement debacle, then went into executive session.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors outlined its schedule for processing a late batch of abatement applications and explained to residents the 90-day window to negotiate with the board before filing with the Appellate Tax Board. The board reorganized and kept its current chair, which drew sharp criticism from a resident. The board then moved to a roll-call vote to enter executive session on abatement applications, and the meeting closed.

public_comment.topic: Resident (addressed as Dave McDonald) asked whether people were still being called to attend; board said piecemeal batches mean limited remote slots per meeting.
Resident asked about a dwelling value rising and how to challenge a discrepancy, and whether to go straight to the Appellate Tax Board.

Dave asked how to tell residents they have 90 days to talk to the board before filing with the Appellate Tax Board, and asked for written guidance to pass along; also asked that the abatement letter be made clearer.
Resident of Ruth Street asked whether possible errors submitted on property cards, including a duplicate tax bill, would be reviewed with the abatement; told yes.

Dave asked the board to reconsider re-electing the chair and urged new leadership, criticising the town's handling of the abatements; also asked about interest on abatement refunds and mentioned families who sold their homes.

The board has processed applications at a pace per hour and estimates several more meetings to finish, to get tax bills out on time.

what_happened.line: The board kept its current chair in a reorganization vote, passed by voice with the count not audible.
A resident urged the board to reconsider and choose new leadership, criticising the town's handling of the abatements; the vote stood.
The board set remote abatement-processing meetings for four June dates, aiming to finish by the 15th so tax bills mail on time.
The board affirmed residents may contact it first during the 90 days before filing with the Appellate Tax Board, and said it would provide a state appeals guide.
The board then moved by roll call into executive session on abatement applications, and the meeting closed.

why_it_matters: Property owners with a disputed valuation or a possible error on their property card have a 90-day window to resolve it with the board before an Appellate Tax Board filing, and the board's June 15 target decides whether abatements are settled before tax bills mail.
Abatement refunds wait on the work reaching accounting, and the board did not yet know what interest would be paid, so when refunds arrive and in what amount remain open.
watch_next: Remote abatement-processing meetings on June 7, 8, 13 and 15, with completion targeted for the 15th.
The state tax appeals guide the board said it would provide for the residents' committee.
